profile.reading:
This OpenStreetMap point sits roughly 40 feet from a sibling point also named simply STACK Infrastructure at the same San Jose, California location, a distance small enough that the two are best read as two mapped suites in one building rather than two separate facilities. That sibling point's own OpenStreetMap tags place the pair at 2150 Trade Zone Boulevard, San Jose, California 95131, distinguishing a level 0 unit 107 from a level 1 unit 201, and this record is treated here as the second of that pair rather than as an independent duplicate campus entry. The City of San Jose parcel layer returns assessor parcel 244-17-011 at this point, zoned IP for industrial park use, within the North San Jose planning area, with San Jose Water Company as the water provider of record.

STACK Infrastructure, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, publishes its Silicon Valley presence as three campuses spanning 97 acres and 150 megawatts combined, but names and details only two of them on its own site, SVY01 in San Jose at 100 megawatts and SVY02 in Santa Clara at 48 megawatts, a gap of roughly two megawatts against the stated total that most plausibly points to an undisclosed or not yet announced third site rather than to an arithmetic error. For SVY01 specifically, STACK's own page gives 19 acres across four buildings, broken out as SVY01A at 9 megawatts and 140,000 square feet, SVY01B at 32 megawatts and 240,000 square feet, SVY01C at 36 megawatts and 350,000 square feet, and SVY01D at 24 megawatts and 300,000 square feet. STACK's own copy calls the surrounding area among the most constrained development regions in Silicon Valley, language consistent with well documented land, power and water limits on new data center construction across San Jose and neighboring Santa Clara. Nothing in STACK's public materials assigns a suite level address to one of those four lettered buildings, so this record cannot be matched to a specific SVY01A through D building, and no floor area or megawatt figure is written to this row for that reason.

The far better documented power record for this immediate area belongs to a different, adjacent parcel rather than to this building. STACK filed with the California Energy Commission for a small power plant exemption under docket 21-SPPE-02, the STACK Trade Zone Park project, covering separate assessor parcels at 2400 Ringwood Avenue and 1849 Fortune Drive about two tenths of a mile to the west. That filing describes two data center buildings, roughly 522,000 square feet between them, delivering 60 megawatts to information technology equipment, a maximum design electrical load near 90 megawatts on a worst case day, and 91 megawatts of diesel fired standby generation, with Pacific Gas and Electric building a new substation to serve it. The Energy Commission certified that project's environmental review and granted the exemption on April 12, 2023. Those three figures, IT load, utility service, and standby generation, belong to that neighboring parcel and not to this suite, and are recorded here only as regional context.

San Jose requires a special use permit for any data center use and a separate special use permit for large energy projects of 20 megawatts or more, and as of mid 2026 the city was drafting uniform citywide standards covering energy sourcing, water use, air quality and greenhouse gas emissions for such projects. What remains unknown for this specific suite is which SVY01 building it sits within, whether STACK owns or leases the address outright, and any power or floor area figure attributable to it alone.
profile.campus_note: One of 2 buildings OpenStreetMap contributors have mapped under this name in this locality, numbered west to east.
profile.research_note: Verified 2026-09-06. Coordinate check against sibling node osm:node/8238715059 (lat 37.4027449, lon -121.891051 vs this row's 37.4026341, -121.891057) puts the two about 12 meters (roughly 40 feet) apart, matching the distance node 059's own reading already attributed to a second suite (unit 201, level 1) at the same 2150 Trade Zone Boulevard address it holds (unit 107, level 0). Conclusion: this is almost certainly that second suite in the same building, not a duplicate OSM mapping of node 059 itself and not an independent building. Prose was written fresh rather than copied from node 059's reading, with different emphasis and sentence structure, per instructions. Cannot confirm which of STACK's four lettered SVY01 buildings (A-D) this suite occupies, so no it_capacity_mw or building_sqft value is set. The CEC docket 21-SPPE-02 figures (60MW IT / ~90MW utility service / 91MW standby diesel) belong to a separate, nearby STACK parcel (Ringwood Ave / Fortune Dr), not this suite, and are recorded strictly as regional context, never as this row's own numeric fields.

reading.body:
STACK Infrastructure operates a 100-megawatt data center campus in San Jose under the designation SVY01, spread across four buildings on 19 acres in the North San Jose industrial park. The site sits in a region the operator describes as among the most constrained in Silicon Valley for land, power, and water. At 100 megawatts of IT load, assuming 40 kilowatts per rack as a common training density, this translates roughly to 2,500 racks, a scale material to frontier AI training but well below the largest concentrated deployments now entering service.

This specific record maps to one of two suites at 2150 Trade Zone Boulevard and cannot be attributed to any single lettered building or power figure within the SVY01 complex. The operator publishes four buildings at SVY01 with capacities of 9, 32, 36, and 24 megawatts respectively, but has not disclosed which holds this suite. San Jose requires separate special use permits for data center use and for large energy projects above 20 megawatts, and as of mid-2026 was drafting uniform standards for energy sourcing, water use, air quality, and emissions across such facilities.

SVY01 ranks twelfth by published capacity among the 103 data center facilities mapped in California and represents roughly 27 percent of the state's 365 published megawatts. Only 11 of 103 mapped facilities in California publish power specifications, concentrating scrutiny on a thin slice of actual deployed compute. Regional constraints on power, land, and water documented in San Jose make additional capacity expansions here difficult, placing future growth in other markets.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
